title: Backside 50/50
description: A leg entanglement from behind where the attacker controls both the hip line and Knee Line, creating dangerous heel exposure from the rear.
topPlayerGoals: The top player wants to control Backside 50/50 through Head Position, Inside Position, and directed pressure.
Maintain both knee lines, the secondary leg, and safe rotation direction.
Keep a stable base so you are not off-balanced or countered.
bottomPlayerGoals: The bottom player wants to survive Backside 50/50 with frames, Pummeling, or the right angle.
Bring the heel to the hip line, free the secondary leg, and clear the Knee Line before rotating.
Recognize danger signals early instead of waiting for the position to settle.
controlPoints: Main control point: Double trapped Knee Line, heel past hip line, and locked secondary leg.
Head, hands, hips, and knees should share the same force direction.
The Elbow-Knee Connection or hip-shoulder line determines whether the position is still alive or already locked.
escapePriorities: Escape priority: Do not rotate blind, assess Knee Line entrapment and heel exposure first, then act.
Protect the neck, back, Knee Line, or arm line before countering.
If Inside Position is lost, reset one defensive layer first.

advancementOptions.action: Transition to saddle or Heel Hook finish
advancementOptions.why: This is the natural branch when you win the main control point and the opponent is forced to defend.

dangerSignals: The chin or neck is pulled out of a safe line.
The elbow separates from the ribs or knee.
The hip line is locked while the shoulder line is still being pulled.
You need a long hand post to avoid falling.
